title: Dataclass-first streaming models + idempotent-retry playbook for Python SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a dataclass-first parsing strategy for the Python SDK structured output helpers that is optimized for streaming use-cases, and publish a concise idempotent-retry playbook for SDK consumers to avoid duplicate side-effects when retrying streamed responses.

Motivation: Many callers prefer lightweight dataclass models for runtime performance and predictable memory usage, especially when processing high-throughput streaming LLM responses (embeddings, token streams with structured events). Current SDK helpers favor pydantic-heavy validation which increases parse latency and memory churn during stream assembly. We need a hybrid approach: dataclass-first fast path + optional pydantic validation on checkpoint boundaries. Additionally, streaming retries require clear guidance (and primitives) to preserve idempotency for server-side actions triggered by parsed output.

Goals:
- Add a dataclass-first streaming parser that incrementally assembles events and emits typed objects as soon as possible.
- Provide a clear fallback to pydantic validation for users that need strict enforcement (off by default).
- Ship helper utilities: IdempotencyToken generator, checkpointed-replay adapter, and a small retry-playbook in the SDK docs.
- Ensure backward compatibility with existing public SDK response APIs and streaming async iterator ergonomics.

Non-goals:
- Replacing full pydantic-first APIs today; this is an opt-in alternative path.

Example sketch (consumer ergonomics):

from redwood_sdk.streams import DataclassStreamParser, IdempotentReplayAdapter
from models import ThermostatEvent  # small dataclass used in examples

parser = DataclassStreamParser(ThermostatEvent, validate_on_checkpoint=False)
adapter = IdempotentReplayAdapter(client, idempotency_key=make_token())

async for event in adapter.stream(parse=parser):
    if event.type == "temperature_change":
        store_metric(event)
decisions: Dataclass-first path: primary parse path returns dataclass instances with minimal validation to keep latency low.
Validation-on-checkpoint: run optional pydantic models at user-defined checkpoints for strict contracts.
Expose a small helper API for idempotency tokens and checkpointed replay; do not bake server-side guarantees.
Keep public streaming iterator signature unchanged (async iterator of typed objects) to avoid churn.
Backpressure: parser will surface a low-watermark callback so consumers can apply flow control without blocking the runtime thread.
acceptance_criteria: A DataclassStreamParser implemented and unit-tested with at least 90% coverage for incremental framing/assembly.
Benchmarks show median parse latency improvement >= 35% vs current pydantic-first parser on 2k token streams.
IdempotentReplayAdapter provided with example usage and integration tests that simulate mid-stream failures and replay semantics.
Documentation page (SDK docs) added with a retry-playbook and at least two end-to-end examples (thermostat events and order-webhook replays).
No public API breaking changes; old parsing helpers continue to work when users opt in.

implementation_risks: Dataclass-only path may miss subtle user validation needs; mitigated by on-checkpoint pydantic validation.
Framing assumptions across different transports (unix sockets vs HTTP/2) — integration tests added.
Users performing side-effects during streaming may still need server-side guarantees; docs must be explicit about limits.
